name: Ilioinguinal Neuralgia
definition: Neuropathic pain involving the ilioinguinal nerve, commonly after lower abdominal or inguinal surgery, trauma or entrapment.

typical: Pain near inguinal canal or scar

investigations.principle: Usually clinical; ultrasound/MRI and diagnostic block are selective.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, infection, tumor or occult-injury assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Persistent post-surgical entrapment may require nerve specialist review.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Vankshana Vata-neuralgic phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Neuropathic pain involving the ilioinguinal nerve, commonly after lower abdominal or inguinal surgery, trauma or entrapment.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe vascular symptoms, major trauma, suspected infection, pathological fracture, neurovascular compromise or other listed red flags.
